title: Predictors of Lethal Outcome in Patients with Refractory Septic Shock

sections.heading: Predictors of Lethal Outcome in Patients with Refractory Septic Shock
sections.text:
A. A. KOCHKIN 1 , M. Ya. YADGAROV 2 , L. B. BERIKASHVILI 2 , S. N. PEREKHODOV 3 , V. V. LIKHVANTSEV 1,2
1 Moscow Regional Research Clinical Institute named after M. F. Vladimirsky, Moscow, RF

3 A. I. Evdokimov Moscow State University of Medicine and Dentistry, Moscow, RF

Early prediction of disease severity helps the clinician prevent undesirable development of events and/or minimize losses in case of life-threatening complications. This principle fully applies to the situation of refractory septic shock, in which noradrenaline administration at a dose exceeding 0.5 μg · kg -1 · min -1 is necessary to maintain mean arterial pressure.

Objective: to determine predictors of fatal outcome in patients with refractory septic shock.

Materials and methods. A retrospective study included 79 patients with refractory septic shock aged 42 to 74 years (59.7 ± 7.8 years) with disease severity on the SOFA scale from 8 to 16 points. The prognostic significance of indicators was assessed through univariate and multivariate analysis.

Results. In multivariate analysis, SOFA score was the only significant predictor of adverse outcome (adj. OR 1.626 [95% CI 1.313; 2.014], p < 0.001). Other presumed indicators (age, P/F ratio, lactate concentration and procalcitonin level, noradrenaline dose) did not demonstrate predictive ability.

Conclusion. SOFA score is an independent predictor of mortality in adult patients with refractory septic shock (adj. OR 1.26 [95% CI 1.313; 2.014], p < 0.001). According to ROC-analysis results, along with SOFA, noradrenaline dose is also a significant predictor (AUC 0.989 [95% CI 0.934; 1.000], p < 0.001).

Keywords: septic shock, predictors of mortality in septic shock, refractory shock

Early prediction of disease severity helps clinicians prevent adverse events and/or minimize losses in the event of a life-threatening complication. This provision fully applies to refractory septic shock, in which norepinephrine administration at a dose exceeding 0.5 μg/kg-1/min-1 is needed to maintain mean arterial pressure.

The objective: to determine predictors of lethal outcomes in patients with refractory septic shock.

Subjects and methods. A retrospective study included 79 patients with refractory septic shock aged from 42 to 74 years (59.7 ± 7.8), with severity of the condition as per SOFA varying from 8 to 16 scores. The predictive value of indicators was assessed using univariate and multivariate analyses.

Results. In multivariate analysis, the only significant predictor of an unfavorable outcome was the SOFA score (adj. OR: 1.626 [95% CI: 1.313; 2.014], p < 0.001). Other putative indicators (age, oxygenation index, lactate and procalcitonin concentrations, and norepinephrine dose) had no predictive value.

Conclusion: The SOFA score is an independent predictor of lethality in adult patients with refractory septic shock (adj. OR: 1.26 [95% CI: 1.313; 2.014], p < 0.001). According to the results of the ROC analysis, along with SOFA, norepinephrine dose was also a significant predictor (AUC 0.989 [95% CI 0.934; 1.000], p < 0.001).

Key words: septic shock, predictors of lethality in septic shock, refractory shock

Mortality from sepsis and septic shock, despite the introduction of new diagnostic and treatment methods, remains sufficiently high to this day, reaching 40% and more [5]. This aspect makes the problem of improving the results of therapy for sepsis and septic shock one of the most urgent tasks of modern reanimatology. With each passing year, the number of publications devoted to this problem increases: the role of putative markers is proposed for mean arterial pressure [9], the value of VIS (Vasopressor-Inotropic Score) [1], lactate concentration [6], and most often the degree of organ dysfunction, assessed by the SOFA scale [3, 12].

The most severe variant of sepsis is septic shock [10]. Refractory shock is not distinguished as a separate variant of this condition; however, it is precisely this that causes the greatest difficulties in terms of treatment and the most serious concerns regarding prognosis [7, 8]. In this connection, the need for the earliest possible prediction of an unfavorable outcome precisely in patients of this category is evident.

Objective: to determine predictors of lethal outcome in patients with refractory septic shock.

sections.heading: Materials and Methods
Results
sections.text:
Among the studied patients, 28-day mortality was 44% (35 patients). Of these, 17% (6 patients) of adverse outcomes occurred within the first three days. In the overall structure, the primary focus was located in the lungs in 55% of cases, in the abdominal cavity in 35% of cases, and undetermined location of the primary focus and other localizations accounted for 5%.

The main causes of fatal outcomes were: progression of cardiovascular insufficiency - 85% (30 patients); disseminated intravascular coagulation syndrome - 11% (4 patients); progression of respiratory insufficiency against the background of acute respiratory distress syndrome - 3% (1 patient).

The ROC-analysis performed revealed a number of significant quantitative predictors of fatal outcome (Fig. 1).

Fig. 1. Univariate analysis: ROC-curves - assessing the significance of quantitative predictors of lethality

1. Age - AUC 0.670 [95% CI 0.550; 0.790], p = 0.01. Age over 57 years was a risk factor for fatal outcome with sensitivity 80.0% and specificity 56.8%.

2. Increased arterial blood lactate concentration - AUC 0.808 [95% CI 0.712; 0.905], p < 0.001. Lactate concentration exceeding 4.6 mmol/l predicted the risk of fatal outcome with sensitivity 65.7% and specificity 90.9%.

3. Increased dose of noradrenaline required to maintain mean arterial pressure above 65 mm Hg - AUC 0.745 [95% CI 0.634; 0.836], p < 0.0001. Exceeding a dose of 0.57 μg · kg⁻¹ · min⁻¹ was a predictor of adverse outcome with sensitivity 71.4% and specificity 81.8%.

4. Increased procalcitonin concentration - AUC 0.950 [95% CI 0.899; 1.000], p < 0.001. An increase in the indicator > 14.1 ng/ml predicted fatal outcome with sensitivity 85.71% and specificity 100%.

5. P/F ratio - AUC 0.756 [95% CI 0.647; 0.866], p < 0.0001. A decrease in the indicator below 184 mm Hg predicted fatal outcome with sensitivity 65.7% and specificity 81.8% (Fig. 2).

However, the most significant predictor according to ROC-analysis was the indicator "worsening of the degree of organ failure according to the scale

SOFA score" - AUC 0.984 [95% CI 0.964; 1.000], p < 0.001. A score above 11 points predicted an unfavorable outcome with sensitivity of 94.3% and specificity of 93.2% (Fig. 1).

When assessing qualitative (binary) predictors of 28-day mortality, no effect was found for such variables as "need for renal replacement therapy" (p = 0.443) and "use of additional vasopressor drugs" (p = 0.882).

The only comorbid condition that was a significant predictor of lethal outcome in patients with refractory septic shock was the presence of diabetes mellitus (p < 0.001). Among patients with diabetes mellitus who experienced refractory septic shock, 28-day mortality was 100%, whereas mortality in patients without diabetes was 33.3% (Table 1).

According to multivariate analysis results, the only significant predictor of lethal outcome was the SOFA score (adj. OR 1.626 [95% CI 1.313; 2.014], p < 0.001) (Table 2). With each 1-point increase in SOFA, the risk of lethal outcome in patients with refractory septic shock increases by 62.6%.

Additionally, a comparative analysis was conducted on the informativity of two variables: the dose of norepinephrine required to maintain target hemodynamic parameters and SOFA - results are presented in Table 3.

The obtained data did not allow confirmation of the prognostic significance of norepinephrine dose as a predictor of lethal outcome in refractory septic shock (adj. OR 1.024 [95% CI 0.999; 1.050], p = 0.058).

A more accurate and reliable prognosis of lethal outcome was provided by joint analysis of SOFA score and the dose of vasopressor support with norepinephrine (AUC 0.989 [95% CI 0.934; 1.000], p < 0.001).

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text:
Thus, the only significant independent predictor of mortality in patients with refractory septic shock is the SOFA score. Good quality of the prognostic model of this factor regarding mortality was demonstrated based on ROC analysis in the study by Thomas-Rueddel D. O. et al. (AUC 0.686 [95% CI 0.661; 0.710], p < 0.001 [11], AUC 0.74 [95% CI 0.730; 0.760] [13]). In the discussed study, excellent quality of the prognostic factor was demonstrated (AUC 0.984 [95% CI 0.964; 1.000], p < 0.001), which apparently is due to the fact that patients included in this study had a more pronounced degree of organ failure.

The remaining presumed predictors previously identified during univariate analysis did not demonstrate their significance. The absence of statistical significance of the P/F ratio in this case is explained by the fact that these indicators are taken into account when assessing SOFA and therefore are inferior to it in terms of sensitivity/specificity.

Apparently, for the same reason there is no statistical significance of the need for renal replacement therapy - assessment of renal failure is provided for in the SOFA scale.

The absence of a significant role of lactate in multivariate analysis may be due to the fact that assessment of hypoxemia leading to activation of anaerobic glycolysis is provided for in the same SOFA scale [11].

The prognostic significance of noradrenaline dose was not demonstrated in the present study during multivariate regression analysis. Thus, we were unable to confirm the data of T. Auchet et al., who argued that noradrenaline dose is an independent predictor of mortality based on both ROC analysis including 106 patients (AUC 0.760 [95% CI 0.66; 0.86], p < 0.001) and logistic regression analysis (OR 6.04 [95% CI 2.2; 15.06], p < 0.01) [4]. This may be due to insufficient sample size of the discussed study.

It would be desirable to draw attention to one more important fact. The results of multivariate analysis did not confirm the high prognostic significance of a number of studied indicators which apparently demonstrated such significance based on univariate analysis results. This allows us to say that one cannot fully rely only on the results of univariate analysis. In some situations, only multivariate analysis is able to put in their proper place, including the presumed predictors of adverse outcome.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text:
1. SOFA score assessment is an independent predictor of mortality in adult patients with refractory septic shock (adj. OR 1.626 [95% CI 1.313; 2.014], p < 0.001).
2. According to ROC analysis results, along with SOFA, noradrenaline dose is also a significant predictor (AUC 0.989 [95% CI 0.934; 1.000], p < 0.001).

Refractory shock is not distinguished as a separate variant of this condition; however, it is precisely this that causes the greatest difficulties in terms of treatment and the most serious concerns regarding prognosis [7, 8]. In this connection, the need for the earliest possible prediction of an unfavorable outcome precisely in patients of this category is evident.

Objective: to determine predictors of lethal outcome in patients with refractory septic shock.
Materials and Methods
Retrospectively analyzed examination and treatment data of patients with sepsis who developed refractory septic shock. A total of 79 patient medical records were studied (48 men and 31 women) aged 42 to 74 years (59.7 ± 7.8); the degree of organ dysfunction assessed by the SOFA scale ranged from 8 to 16 points. Sepsis was diagnosed based on the "Sepsis-3" criteria [10].

Septic shock was considered refractory when infusion of noradrenaline at a rate exceeding 0.5 μg · kg⁻¹ · min⁻¹ was required to maintain mean arterial pressure above 65 mm Hg [1].

Inclusion criteria for the study:
- established diagnosis of septic shock with need for vasopressor support with noradrenaline at a dose ≥ 0.5 μg · kg⁻¹ · min⁻¹;
- time interval no more than 24 hours from the onset of septic shock;
- duration of mechanical ventilation at the time of inclusion in the study no more than 24 hours;
- signed informed consent to participate in the study.

Exclusion criteria:
- oncological disease;
- pregnancy;
- hemodynamically significant cardiac defects.

Withdrawal criteria:
- massive blood loss as a complication of surgical intervention performed during the study;
- recurrent (after a "lucid interval") development of septic shock during hospitalization.

Intensive care of septic shock was based on the recommendations of the 'Surviving Sepsis Campaign' [10]. Mortality was defined as the occurrence of this event within 28 days from the onset of disease.

The values of indicators measured on day 1 after vasopressor administration, i.e., no later than 24 hours after diagnosis of septic shock, were included in the analysis.

Data accumulation and preliminary analysis were performed using Excel 2019 spreadsheet software; statistical data analysis was performed using IBM SPSS Statistics 25.0 software package and online calculators (https://medstatistic.ru/calculators/calchi.html). To clarify the applicability of parametric tools, the correspondence of variable distribution to the normal law was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test with Lilliefors correction; equality of variances was tested using Levene's test. Based on the results of this assessment, it was found that parametric comparison criteria were not applicable for many indicators due to the small number of outcomes; therefore, comparative between-group analysis was performed using nonparametric statistics. Data description, characteristics of position and dispersion were presented using median and mean value, standard deviation, quartiles, and range.

Comparison of groups by binary variables was performed using Fisher's exact F-test. The confidence interval for frequencies was calculated using the Wald method with Agresti-Coull correction. The significance level at which the null hypothesis of no differences between the studied groups was rejected was chosen as 0.05 [2].

Risk assessment of outcome in univariate analysis was performed using the RR indicator (relative risk, risk ratio) and its 95% confidence interval for each studied predictor. Assessment of 'adjusted odds ratio' was performed in multivariate regression analysis to account for the influence of other factors on risk (age, sex, and confounding variables). To assess the quality of various quantitative indicators as predictors of fatal outcome, ROC analysis was used with assessment of the AUC parameter (area under the ROC curve).
Results
Among the studied patients, 28-day mortality was 44% (35 patients). Of these, 17% (6 patients) of adverse outcomes occurred within the first three days. In the overall structure, the primary focus was located in the lungs in 55% of cases, in the abdominal cavity in 35% of cases, and undetermined location of the primary focus and other localizations accounted for 5%.

The main causes of fatal outcomes were: progression of cardiovascular insufficiency - 85% (30 patients); disseminated intravascular coagulation syndrome - 11% (4 patients); progression of respiratory insufficiency against the background of acute respiratory distress syndrome - 3% (1 patient).

The ROC-analysis performed revealed a number of significant quantitative predictors of fatal outcome (Fig. 1).

Fig. 1. Univariate analysis: ROC-curves - assessing the significance of quantitative predictors of lethality

1. Age - AUC 0.670 [95% CI 0.550; 0.790], p = 0.01. Age over 57 years was a risk factor for fatal outcome with sensitivity 80.0% and specificity 56.8%.

2. Increased arterial blood lactate concentration - AUC 0.808 [95% CI 0.712; 0.905], p < 0.001. Lactate concentration exceeding 4.6 mmol/l predicted the risk of fatal outcome with sensitivity 65.7% and specificity 90.9%.

3. Increased dose of noradrenaline required to maintain mean arterial pressure above 65 mm Hg - AUC 0.745 [95% CI 0.634; 0.836], p < 0.0001. Exceeding a dose of 0.57 μg · kg⁻¹ · min⁻¹ was a predictor of adverse outcome with sensitivity 71.4% and specificity 81.8%.

4. Increased procalcitonin concentration - AUC 0.950 [95% CI 0.899; 1.000], p < 0.001. An increase in the indicator > 14.1 ng/ml predicted fatal outcome with sensitivity 85.71% and specificity 100%.

5. P/F ratio - AUC 0.756 [95% CI 0.647; 0.866], p < 0.0001. A decrease in the indicator below 184 mm Hg predicted fatal outcome with sensitivity 65.7% and specificity 81.8% (Fig. 2).

However, the most significant predictor according to ROC-analysis was the indicator "worsening of the degree of organ failure according to the scale
Oxygenation index
100-Specificity
Fig. 2. ROC-curve - assessment of the significance of oxygenation index as a predictor of lethal outcomes

SOFA score" - AUC 0.984 [95% CI 0.964; 1.000], p < 0.001. A score above 11 points predicted an unfavorable outcome with sensitivity of 94.3% and specificity of 93.2% (Fig. 1).

When assessing qualitative (binary) predictors of 28-day mortality, no effect was found for such variables as "need for renal replacement therapy" (p = 0.443) and "use of additional vasopressor drugs" (p = 0.882).

The only comorbid condition that was a significant predictor of lethal outcome in patients with refractory septic shock was the presence of diabetes mellitus (p < 0.001). Among patients with diabetes mellitus who experienced refractory septic shock, 28-day mortality was 100%, whereas mortality in patients without diabetes was 33.3% (Table 1).

According to multivariate analysis results, the only significant predictor of lethal outcome was the SOFA score (adj. OR 1.626 [95% CI 1.313; 2.014], p < 0.001) (Table 2). With each 1-point increase in SOFA, the risk of lethal outcome in patients with refractory septic shock increases by 62.6%.

Additionally, a comparative analysis was conducted on the informativity of two variables: the dose of norepinephrine required to maintain target hemodynamic parameters and SOFA - results are presented in Table 3.

The obtained data did not allow confirmation of the prognostic significance of norepinephrine dose as a predictor of lethal outcome in refractory septic shock (adj. OR 1.024 [95% CI 0.999; 1.050], p = 0.058).

A more accurate and reliable prognosis of lethal outcome was provided by joint analysis of SOFA score and the dose of vasopressor support with norepinephrine (AUC 0.989 [95% CI 0.934; 1.000], p < 0.001).
Discussion
Thus, the only significant independent predictor of mortality in patients with refractory septic shock is the SOFA score. Good quality of the prognostic model of this factor regarding mortality was demonstrated based on ROC analysis in the study by Thomas-Rueddel D. O. et al. (AUC 0.686 [95% CI 0.661; 0.710], p < 0.001 [11], AUC 0.74 [95% CI 0.730; 0.760] [13]). In the discussed study, excellent quality of the prognostic factor was demonstrated (AUC 0.984 [95% CI 0.964; 1.000], p < 0.001), which apparently is due to the fact that patients included in this study had a more pronounced degree of organ failure.

The remaining presumed predictors previously identified during univariate analysis did not demonstrate their significance. The absence of statistical significance of the P/F ratio in this case is explained by the fact that these indicators are taken into account when assessing SOFA and therefore are inferior to it in terms of sensitivity/specificity.

Apparently, for the same reason there is no statistical significance of the need for renal replacement therapy - assessment of renal failure is provided for in the SOFA scale.

The absence of a significant role of lactate in multivariate analysis may be due to the fact that assessment of hypoxemia leading to activation of anaerobic glycolysis is provided for in the same SOFA scale [11].

The prognostic significance of noradrenaline dose was not demonstrated in the present study during multivariate regression analysis. Thus, we were unable to confirm the data of T. Auchet et al., who argued that noradrenaline dose is an independent predictor of mortality based on both ROC analysis including 106 patients (AUC 0.760 [95% CI 0.66; 0.86], p < 0.001) and logistic regression analysis (OR 6.04 [95% CI 2.2; 15.06], p < 0.01) [4]. This may be due to insufficient sample size of the discussed study.

It would be desirable to draw attention to one more important fact. The results of multivariate analysis did not confirm the high prognostic significance of a number of studied indicators which apparently demonstrated such significance based on univariate analysis results. This allows us to say that one cannot fully rely only on the results of univariate analysis. In some situations, only multivariate analysis is able to put in their proper place, including the presumed predictors of adverse outcome.
Conclusions
1. SOFA score assessment is an independent predictor of mortality in adult patients with refractory septic shock (adj. OR 1.626 [95% CI 1.313; 2.014], p < 0.001).
2. According to ROC analysis results, along with SOFA, noradrenaline dose is also a significant predictor (AUC 0.989 [95% CI 0.934; 1.000], p < 0.001).

original_sections.text:

1 Московский областной научно-исследовательский клинический институт им. М. Ф. Владимирского, Москва, РФ

Раннее прогнозирование тяжести течения заболевания помогает клиницисту предотвратить нежелательное развитие событий и(или) минимизировать потери в случае наступления жизнеугрожающего осложнения� Данное положение в полной мере относится к ситуации рефрактерного септического шока, при котором для поддержания среднего артериального давления необходимо введение норадреналина в дозе более 0,5 мкг · кг -1 · мин -1 �
Цель: определить предикторы летального исхода у пациентов в состоянии рефрактерного септического шока�
Материалы и методы. В ретроспективное исследование включено 79 пациентов в состоянии рефрактерного септического шока в возрасте от 42 до 74 лет (59,7 ± 7,8 года) с тяжестью состояния по шкале SOFA от 8 до 16 баллов� Прогностическую значимость показателей оценивали в ходе одномерного и многомерного анализа�
Результаты. В многомерном анализе единственным значимым предиктором неблагоприятного исхода оказалась оценка по шкале SOFA (аdj� OR 1,626 [95%-ный ДИ 1,313; 2,014], p < 0,001)� У других предполагаемых показателей (возраст, соотношение P/F, концентрации лактата и уровень прокальцитонина, доза норадреналина) предикторная способность не выявлена�
Вывод. Оценка по шкале SOFA является независимым предиктором летальности у взрослых пациентов с рефрактерным септическим шоком (аdj� OR 1,26 [95%-ный ДИ 1,313; 2,014], p < 0,001)� По результатам ROC-анализа, наряду с SOFA, значимым предиктором является и доза норадреналина (AUC 0,989 [95%-ный ДИ 0,934; 1,000], p < 0,001)�

Early prediction of disease severity helps clinicians prevent adverse events and/or minimize losses in the event of a life-threatening complication� This provision fully applies to refractory septic shock, in which norepinephrine administration at a dose exceeding 0�5 μ g/kg -1 /min -1 is needed to maintain mean arterial pressure�
The objective: to determine predictors of lethal outcomes in patients with refractory septic shock�
Subjects and methods. A retrospective study included 79 patients with refractory septic shock aged from 42 to 74 years (59�7 ± 7�8), with severity of the condition as per SOF A varying from 8 to 16 scores�  The predictive value of indicators was assessed using univariate and multivariate analyses�
Results. In multivariate analysis, the only significant predictor of an unfavorable outcome was the SOF A score (adj�  OR: 1�626 [95% CI: 1�313; 2�014], p < 0�001)�  Other putative indicators (age, oxygenation index, lactate and procalcitonin concentrations, and norepinephrine dose) had no predictive value�
Conclusion: The SOFA score is an independent predictor of lethality in adult patients with refractory septic shock (аdj� OR: 1�26 [95% CI: 1�313; 2�014], p < 0�001)� According to the results of the ROC analysis, along with SOF A, norepinephrine dose was also a significant predictor (AUC 0�989 [95% CI 0�934; 1�000], p < 0�001)�
Key words: septic shock, predictors of lethality in septic shock, refractory shock

Летальность от сепсиса и септического шока, несмотря на внедрение новых методик диагностики и лечения, и по сей день остается достаточно высокой, достигая 40% и более [5]� Данный аспект делает проблему улучшения результатов терапии сепсиса и септического шока одной из наиболее
Correspondence: Aleksandr A� Kochkin Email: favor2991@mail�ru
актуальных задач современной реаниматологии� С каждым годом увеличивается число публикаций, посвященных этой проблеме: на роль предполагаемых маркеров предлагаются среднее артериальное давление [9], величина VIS (Vasopressor-Inotropic Score) [1], концентрация лактата [6] и чаще всего
степень органной дисфункции, оцениваемая по шкале SOFA [3, 12]�
Наиболее тяжелым вариантом течения сепсиса является септический шок [10]� Рефрактерный шок не выделяется как отдельный вариант течения данного состояния, однако именно он вызывает наибольшие затруднения в плане лечения и самые тяжелые опасения в плане прогноза [7, 8]� В этой связи очевидна необходимость возможно более раннего прогнозирования наступления неблагоприятного исхода именно у больных этой категории�
Цель: определить предикторы летального исхода у пациентов в состоянии рефрактерного септического шока�

original_sections.heading: Обсуждение
original_sections.text:
Итак, единственным значимым, независимым предиктором летального исхода у пациентов с рефрактерным септическим шоком является оценка по шкале SOFA� Хорошее качество прогностической модели фактора в отношении летального исхода продемонстрировано на основании ROC-анализа в ходе исследовании Thomas-Rueddel D� O� et al� (AUC 0,686 [95%-ный ДИ 0,661; 0,710], p < 0,001 [11], AUC 0,74 [95%-ный ДИ 0,730; 0,760] [13])� В ходе обсуждаемого исследования продемонстрировано отличное качество прогностического фактора (AUC 0,984 [95%-ный ДИ 0,964; 1,000], p < 0,001), что, по всей видимости, обусловлено тем, что пациенты, включенные в данное исследование, имели более выраженную степень органной недостаточности�
Остальные предполагаемые предикторы, ранее выявленные в процессе проведения одномерного анализа, не продемонстрировали своей значимости� Отсутствие статистической значимости отношения P/F в данном случае объясняется тем, что данные показатели учитываются при оценке по SOFA и потому уступают последней по показателям чувствительность/специфичность�
По-видимому, по той же причине отсутствует статистическая значимость потребности в заместительной почечной терапии - оценка почечной недостаточности предусмотрена в шкале SOFA�
Отсутствие значимой роли лактата в многофакторном анализе, возможно, обусловлено тем, что оценка гипоксемии, приводящей к активации анаэробного гликолиза, предусмотрена все той же шкалой SOFA [11]�
Прогностическая значимость дозы норадреналина  не  продемонстрирована  в  ходе  настоящего  исследования  при  проведении  многомерного  регрессионного анализа� Таким образом, нам не  удалось  подтвердить данные T� Auchet et al�, утверждавших, что доза норадреналина является независимым предиктором летальности на основа-
нии как ROC-анализа, включившего 106 пациентов (AUC  0,760 [95%-ный ДИ 0,66; 0,86], p < 0,001), так и логистического регрессионного анализа (OR 6,04 [95%-ный ДИ 2,2; 15,06], p < 0,01) [4]� Возможно, виной тому недостаточный объем выборки обсуждаемого исследования�
Хотелось бы обратить внимание еще на один важный факт� Результаты многомерного анализа не подтвердили высокой прогностической значимости ряда изученных показателей, которые, вроде бы, продемонстрировали таковую по результатам одномерного анализа� Это позволяет говорить о том, что нельзя полностью полагаться только на результаты одномерного анализа� В некоторых ситуациях толь-
ко многомерный анализ в состоянии расставить по местам, в том числе и предполагаемые предикторы неблагоприятного исхода�
